No. 29: Oklahoma City Thunder

June 26 Update: On talent, Ledo is probably a lottery pick. He's a pure scorer who may be one of the best shooters in the draft. But his troubled off-the-court life combined with missing a year because of NCAA issues hurts both his stock and his future.

Quick fact: Did not play in 2012-13.

June 25 Update: This might be a bit of a reach. But the Thunder have been looking for an elite shooting guard, and Ledo is as talented as several players in the lottery. He has lots of off-court issues, but the Thunder might try to rehabilitate him in their excellent D-League franchise.

June 24 Update: Ledo would likely be ranked much higher if there weren't serious off-court concerns. He's the last player on the board to garner a rating of 8 for our Secret NBA Draft Big Board, but he also racked up a number of 2 and 3 ratings from teams. He could be this year's Lance Stephenson. His draft night range is 24 to 35.

June 18 Update: Ledo continues to draw praise from every team for which he works out. The Clippers appear to be especially high on him. I think Ledo could end up going higher (maybe even much higher) on draft night. A few teams in the late lottery and mid-first round are taking a look. But if he lands here, it's a steal for the Clippers, who have a track record of taking young players later in the draft and developing them.

June 10 Update: It's really tough to place Ledo at the moment. He has lottery talent and his workouts, by all accounts, have been very impressive. He's worked out in Boston, Minnesota, Denver, Memphis, New York and Phoenix to fairly rave reviews. Assuming the Suns and Wolves aren't looking at him with their lottery picks, that puts his range at 16-30. I wouldn't count out a team like Boston taking him high. GM Danny Ainge hasn't been afraid to roll the dice on talented young players, and Ledo has one of the highest ceilings in the draft.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 29 pick, Oklahoma City Thunder): Ledo was one of the country's best high school scorers in 2011-12, but he wasn't able to showcase his talents after being ruled academically ineligible by the NCAA. Still, a number of GMs believe he could be a late-first-round steal. With the Thunder going for a safe big man in Dieng at the top of the first round, it might not hurt to roll the dice in the second half.

Apr 9 Update: Ledo announced that he's declaring for the 2013 NBA Draft. Ledo sat out his freshman season and apparently isn't going to give the NCAA another shot to declare him ineligible. Ledo was ranked as the 21st-best high school prospect by ESPN last year and was considered by many scouts to be a potential first-rounder. He's an elite scorer who can hit shots from anywhere on the floor and some scouts project him as a point guard. But with no body of college work outside of the Friars' practice sessions, scouts are all over the place on his stock. He's a likely late first- to second-round pick.

Sept 5 Update: Ledo was ruled a partial qualifier by the NCAA, allowing him to practice but not play this season.

Ledo would still be a potential first round pick if he declares for the 2013 NBA Draft. However, right now he's indicated that he plans to return to Providence for the 2013-14 season.

June 27 Update: Ledo could be the most talented offensive player in the 2012 class. He can score from anywhere on the floor, but his signature move is his step-back, off-the-dribble shot from behind the arc. He knows how to create space and rise up over defenders when he gets in the paint. He can stop on a dime and pull up or continue all the way to get an old-fashioned 3-point play. He is ideal for isolations and when the clock is winding down because he is always ready to score. However, he's going to have to prove he can play with his teammates by not freezing them out on the court and show he can be mature off the floor. -- by Paul Biancardi
Jamal Crawford

The Bucks sent this pick to the Mavs, who then sent it on to Hawks. Ledo has top-10 talent. He's a scoring machine who can really shoot the ball. He slipped after missing the season because the NCAA declared him academically ineligible in addition to numerous off-court issues. If the Hawks can rehabilitate him, he has a chance to be this year's Lance Stephenson.

June 26 Update: Rice is a test case for the D-League. His dominance there has evoked a hot debate about how great stats translate from the D-League to the NBA. Rice is a great athlete and a good shooter, but he's a bit of a tweener.

Quick fact: Rice Jr. led the D-League with 1.18 points per play on guarded catch-and-shoots (min. 50 plays).

June 18 Update: If the Suns get their 2-guard with their first pick, don't be surprised if Phoenix tries to add another wing who can shoot the ball with its second first-rounder. Rice dominated the D-League last season and probably is big enough to spend time at the 3. He's also one of the two or three most NBA-ready prospects in the draft.

June 10 Update: Rice has worked out for the Bucks, Bulls, Rockets, Jazz and Blazers. All three teams are looking for a wing who can shoot the basketball, though the Blazers appear the highest on Rice. In general, teams are all over the board in terms of what they think of him. Some think his dominant performance in the D-League makes him one of the surer things in the draft, while others were disappointed with his performance in the draft combine. It's really tough to peg where he's going at the moment.

May 28 Update: Rice came into the combine facing pretty high expectations, and the general consensus was that he struggled to meet them in Chicago. His shot wasn't falling, and he didn't really stand out in any of the drills or interviews. He's still a likely mid-to-late first-round pick.

May 15 Update: Rice is coming off a terrific performance in the D-League playoffs and finals. He's drawn major attention from NBA scouts and GMs the past few months, and has had the most significant rise of anyone on our Big Board. In Chicago he'll be on the floor with his peers for the first time all season. Athletically, he's going to look great, and he's been shooting the ball very well in the D-League. Interviews will be key. He has some major off-the-court red flags from his past. It appears he's matured quite a bit this season, but teams will be pointed in trying to understand why and how he's grown up this season.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 15 pick, Milwaukee Bucks): We put Rice in our top 30 several months ago after he started getting more minutes in the D-League and broke loose. It wasn't a fluke. Rice led the Rio Grande Vipers to the D-League championship, scoring 25 PPG in the finals. He's a bit of a tweener, but he has NBA athleticism, can really shoot the basketball and is an excellent rebounder for his size. Most importantly, in the D-League he excelled at a high level among elite college players and former NBA rotation guys. He could help the Bucks right away next season.

May 2 Update: Rice may end up being a trailblazer of sorts for American players who can't (or don't) want to take the college route to the NBA. After being dismissed by Georgia Tech last season, Rice ended up with the Rio Grande Vipers in the D-League and has been on an absolute tear since March. He led the Vipers to the D-League championship, averaging 25 points, 9.5 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game in the postseason. He had 25 points and 13 rebounds in the final game. Say what you will about the D-League, but Rice's impressive numbers there make him a virtual lock for the first round, and could end up propelling him several spots higher on our Big Board once teams work him out.

Mar 11 Update: Rice has fallen off the radar since he was dismissed from Georgia Tech before the season began. However he's quietly started making a name for himself in the D League with the Rio Grande Vipers. He's averaging 18.5 ppg and 8 rpg in his last 10 games and was named the NBDL Player of the Week on March 11 when he averaged 24 ppg for the week. While there are questions about his off the court behavior, a number of NBA scouts are looking at him closely as a late first round to second round steal.

The Sixers are trading this pick to the Wizards. The Wizards already took one small forward in Otto Porter, and now they get a second in Rice. Rice dominated the D-League this year, is an elite athlete and shooter. I think he was underrated because of past problems at Georgia Tech. If he's grown up, he's a steal.

June 26 Update: Mitchell is another player who has struggled to live up to his potential. He's an athletic freak with a penchant for rebounding and defending, but his offensive game fell apart as a sophomore and his effort was definitely lacking at times. Still, lots of upside for a player in this range.

Quick fact: When defending isolation sets, Mitchell held his opponent to 1-of-20 from the field.

June 25 Update: Mitchell's been at this spot for three mocks and I continue to hear the Knicks like him. He has all of the physical tools to succeed in the NBA: strength, length, elite athletic ability. And the Knicks really need help on the front line.The Knicks also like Jamaal Franklin, and South Dakota State's Nate Wolters is a sleeper here.

June 24 Update: Mitchell began the season ranked as a potential top-10 pick, but he struggled at North Texas this year and saw the bottom drop out of his stock. While several teams have him rated as a 7 for our Secret NBA Draft Big Board, several other teams see him as a likely bust. His draft night range is 24 to 35.

June 18 Update: I continue to hear the Knicks have a strong affinity for Mitchell. He has all of the physical tools to succeed in the NBA -- strength, length, elite athletic ability. And the Knicks really need help on the front line. I also hear South Dakota State's Nate Wolters is a sleeper here.

June 10 Update: Mitchell is another player who appears to be all over draft boards at the moment. Some teams think he could be the next Kenneth Faried. Others are much more skeptical after a rough sophomore season at North Texas. The Blazers, Nuggets, Jazz and Knicks have all worked him out. The Knicks, I'm told, are especially high on Mitchell. The Knicks don't really have anyone under contract for next season who can back up Amar'e Stoudemire at the 4.

May 28 Update: After a disappointing sophomore season, Mitchell made some serious progress at the combine, showing off better than expected measurements alongside some terrific athleticism. More importantly, he had candid interviews with teams that suddenly made GMs much more comfortable in taking him. Was he just in the wrong situation at North Texas? If teams believe that, he's going to go a lot higher based on his talent.

May 2 Update: Mitchell has hung around this spot for much of the past two months. Teams are intrigued with his potential and disappointed with his production. If he can make a strong push in workouts, someone will take him in the first round.

Apr 2 Update: While Mitchell's season wasn't one to write home about, a number of scouts are predicting he'll increase his draft stock during team workouts and at the NBA draft combine. "The talent is all there," said one NBA scout. "At the very least he's going to rebound and defend for you. I think you for sure gamble with him in the late first round."

Mar 26 Update: Mitchell declared for the NBA draft last week. His season was a major disappointment, but scouts really do like his rebounding and athletic ability. Interviews and workouts will be key to whether he stays in the first round.

Mar 13 Update: Mitchell's disappointing season came to an end Thursday with a loss to Louisiana-Lafayette in the Sun Belt tournament. Although his offensive woes continued, he did put up some strong rebounding and shot-blocking numbers in his last three games, averaging 12 boards and nearly three blocks per game over those last three. Mitchell said he's on the fence about whether to return to North Texas for another season. Given how much his draft stock has plummeted this year, I no longer think it's a foregone conclusion that he'll leave for the NBA.

Feb 27 Update: The "what is wrong with Tony Mitchell?" saga continues. His February has been just horrible. He's averaging 11.3 points per game in that stretch and has struggled to really assert himself on both ends of the floor. He's in real danger of falling out of the first round.

Jan 30 Update: Mitchell had one of his best games of the season last Saturday against Florida Atlantic (24 points, 8 rebounds) before dropping in two more uninspired showings -- a 10-point, 7-turnover performance in a loss against Middle Tennessee followed by a 3-for-9 shooting night against Arkansas-Little Rock. Scouts aren't sure what to do with him at this point. Everyone believes he has NBA talent, but there are legitimate questions about how much he really wants to do anything with it.

Dec 14 Update: No one has been a bigger disappointment than Mitchell for NBA scouts. Mitchell seriously flirted with the draft last year and, had he declared, would have gone somewhere in the mid-to-late first round. Many believed that with another year under his belt, and in the weak Sun Belt league, Mitchell would be putting up player of the year-type numbers this season. Instead, he has regressed a bit as a player. His numbers across the board are down and so are his team's. He is going to need a very strong season to pull himself back into the top 10.

Nov 30 Update: Mitchell came into the season with huge expectations. Many scouts wondered aloud whether he'd be a sure fire top-5 pick if he played at a big school. Many thought he'd put up huge numbers this season. So far, Mitchell has been a major disappointment. His team is just 3-4 and his numbers are down across the board -- lower field goal percentage, shooting just 29 percent from 3, fewer rebounds, fewer assists. Scouts that are making their way to see him in games are all coming back with the same question: Is he really a lottery pick? The answer: Not if he keeps playing this way all season.

Oct 23 Update: Mitchell was an elite prospect coming out of high school, but ran into some academic trouble at Missouri and ended up sitting out the season before transferring to North Texas. He didn't disappoint in his first season with the Mean Green, averaging 14.7 ppg, 10.3 rpg, 3 bpg, and shooting 57 percent from the field.

Virtually everyone in the NBA expected him to declare for the draft after last season, but he surprised them all by returning to school for his sophomore season. If he were at North Carolina or Kentucky, Mitchell would likely be considered for the No. 1 pick in the draft.

He has a rare combination of size, athletic ability and basketball skills on both ends of the floor. Defensively he can be a monster. He's both a terrific rebounder and shot-blocker and can guard multiple positions. Offensively, he's still developing, but has showed talent both as a scorer in the paint and on the perimeter.

The biggest challenge for talent evaluators is the lack of talent Mitchell is playing with and against. There aren't any other NBA-caliber players on his roster, and the toughest team they are scheduled to play all season is Creighton. That said, a small conference and poor competition didn't stop the Blazers from taking Lillard at No. 6, and if Mitchell plays well this season, he has a great shot of even going a spot or two higher than Lillard did in June.

Apr 9 Update: Mitchell is one of the most talented players in the country that very few people know about. Playing at North Texas can do that to you. He was widely expected to declare for the 2012 NBA Draft where he would've been a likely first round pick. However, reports say he's heading back to North Texas. With a great year he could be a late lottery to mid first round pick in 2012.

Mar 9 Update: Mitchell missed a huge opportunity to show off his stuff at the national level when the Mean Green lost to Western Kentucky in the Sun Belt final. Mitchell was solid once again. He's a special player who would, with better exposure, be about 10 spots higher on our board. NBA scouts expect him to declare and if he has great workouts, he could make a major jump up our board. Scouts just need to see him matched up against some talent.

Jan 24 Update: Mitchell is lighting up the Sun Belt conference. Since Mitchell became eligible the Mean Green are 8-3 and Mitchell's averaging 15.5 ppg and 9.4 rpg on 63 percent shooting and 59 percent shooting from behind the arc. And he's getting better. In January he's had a 34- and-14 game versus South Alabama and a 30-point, 17-rebound game versus Denver on Saturday. The competition might not be great, but scouts saw enough talent at the under-19s to believe that Mitchell has a chance to be special. He's cracked our Top 30 for the first time this year and, truthfully, could end up going much higher once he gets into NBA workouts.

Dec 20 Update: Mitchell (Top 100 Rank: 40) played his first game of the season versus Jackson State and had 14 points and 10 rebounds in just 20 minutes. Mitchell is a bit of an enigma to scouts -- more legend than solid production -- but if he plays big for North Texas, he's got a great shot at being a first-round pick.

Nov 17 Update: Mitchell was an elite prospect coming out of high school but ran into some academic trouble at Missouri and ended up sitting out the year before transferring to North Texas, where he remains ineligible until the end of the fall semester. But scouts got excited about him as a player for Team USA in the under-19 worlds. Mitchell wasn't dominant and played just 16 minutes per game, but he showed off his great physical tools and was a factor on the boards and defensive end the entire tournament. He's still a major work in progress on the offensive end. As an athletic rebounder, shot blocker and defender who can guard multiple positions, he's a very intriguing prospect. But he's going to have to improve dramatically on the offensive end to realize his potential.

Jan 18 Update: Mitchell is one of the top-ranked freshmen in the country. But like other phenoms, including Enes Kanter and Renardo Sidney, he's run afoul of the NCAA. This time, grades are the issue, and Mitchell was forced to sit out the fall semester at MU. Now there is more evidence that Mitchell is still struggling to be eligible for the winter semester.

If he can't get his grades up, Mitchell will lose the season and likely head to the draft this spring. It's a shame. Mitchell has a ton of God-given talent. He's long and athletic and can guard and play multiple positions. He also plays with a great motor. But what he needs is more time on the court to improve his offensive game and basketball IQ. Someone in the NBA will draft him based on pure potential, but he's the type of kid who could have really used a year or two of college basketball to polish his game.

The Pistons got a huge steal in Mitchell. He's long, athletic and really rebounds. He struggled as a primary offensive option at North Texas, but as a role player -- on a team like the Pistons -- he's a really great fit. He had lottery talent, so he's a great pick here.

No. 35: Philadelphia 76ers

May 28 Update: Withey didn't do anything extraordinary at the combine, but few expected him to. His main attributes are his height and defense, and neither shows particularly well in the drills. Workouts will be key against Dieng, Adams, Gobert, Plumlee and Olynyk.

May 15 Update: If there was a shot-blocking drill where the goal was to block as many shots as possible without fouling the shooter, Withey would walk away with the prize handily. Alas, the focus on offense probably won't speak to Withey's strengths at the combine. Big men rarely have their stock helped or hurt at the combine -- his real tests will come in workouts against Gorgui Dieng, Steven Adams, Rudy Gobert and Mason Plumlee.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 24 pick, New York Knicks): The Knicks have a strong front line but an aging one. Withey is one of the best two or three shot-blockers in the draft and could immediately help the Knicks' interior defense.

May 2 Update: Withey is suffering from the same sort of malaise that has hit Plumlee. He's a terrific shot-blocker who stays out of foul trouble, but can he be anything more than that at the next level? I'm not sure he'll crack the lottery, but teams with picks just outside the lottery -- such as the Bulls, Jazz and Hawks -- all could use his help.

Apr 2 Update: Withey ended the season with a solid 12-point, 8-rebound, 5-block performance against Michigan. However, he struggled to contain freshman Mitch McGary at times. While Withey had the edge in size and gave McGary problems when he was on the block, McGary's nimbleness proved to be problematic and Withey struggled to get out and guard on the perimeter. Overall, Withey had another excellent season and given his size and shot-blocking ability, should fall somewhere in the range of 15-25 on draft night.

Mar 26 Update: Ben McLemore might get all the love from scouts, but it's been Withey who has carried Kansas on his back the past few weeks with McLemore in a slump. Withey is averaging just under 17 points, eight rebounds and four blocks per game in his last three -- the Big 12 championship game and the first two rounds of the NCAA tournament. He does so quietly but with toughness. He might never be a star offensive player in the league, however his shot blocking and defense should be enough to guarantee him a long life in the NBA as a big man coming off the bench.

Mar 13 Update: Withey has been playing a hyperefficient brand of basketball of late, shooting 23-for-27 from the field in his past four while averaging more than four blocks and nine rebounds per game. He's not a sexy prospect, but Withey could have a long career in the NBA as a shot-blocker off the bench.

Feb 27 Update: Withey is what he is -- an elite shot-blocker, a solid rebounder and a decent offensive player. But given his size and the high level he's performed at the past two seasons, that will get him a spot in the first round.

Jan 30 Update: Withey's slide down two spots doesn't have anything to do with his play. Oladipo and Robinson's moves up the board pushed him down. While scouts aren't convinced Withey has major NBA upside, his rebounding and shot-blocking ability should make him a rotation big man in the league for years.

Nov 30 Update: Withey was a late bloomer who didn't really get a chance to play his first two seasons at KU. His junior year he emerged as one of the best shot-blockers in the country, but still appeared very raw offensively.

This season, Withey has improved in every statistical category. He's averaging nearly 14 points, eight rebounds and five blocks in KU's first five games. His 25-point, seven-block game against Saint Louis this weekend drew raves from scouts in attendance. Again, size matters in the NBA, and as they will with Plumlee, scouts will be willing to overlook some deficiencies in Withey if they believe he can play 15 to 20 minutes a night and defend the rim. Given Withey's development, that doesn't seem out of the question.

Oct 18 Update: Withey was a revelation as a junior last season. He had his coming-out party at the Maui Invitational, and by the end of the season, he was one of the best shot-blocking big men in college basketball.

Withey basically emerged from obscurity last season, so everything he did was gravy. Now, the expectations are much higher. Withey's calling card is on the defensive end. Only Anthony Davis blocked more shots per 40 minutes last season. Offensively, Withey is still a work in progress, though he did show progress last season.

If he can continue to add strength and improve his low-post game, he has a chance to stick in the NBA. The league always needs backup centers, and Withey's defensive abilities should guarantee him a spot somewhere in the late first round.

Apr 19 Update:Withey came out of nowhere to become one of the most dominant shot blocker in the NCAA this year. Had he declared for the draft, he would've been a likely late first round to early second round pick. He takes a risk by coming back, but if he can improve a pretty weak offensive game, he could be a lock for the first round in 2012.

Apr 3 Update: We started writing about Withey as an NBA draft prospect at the Maui Invitational -- but we thought it would be in the 2013 draft. His shot-blocking in the tournament has clearly put him on the NBA's radar screen. He's very limited offensively, but when you block an Anthony Davis shot at the rim you've got a chance. Withey would be better served returning to Kansas for his senior year and working on his post game. But if he did declare (he said after the title game he was returning to Kansas), I think someone would grab him in the second round and hope he can get enough minutes to impact the game on the defensive end.

Feb 21 Update: Coming into the season, Withey was a question mark as a Jayhawks starter, let alone an NBA prospect. We were impressed with him early at the Maui Invitational, but over the past month or so Withey looks like he could be a legitimate NBA first-round prospect. In a three-game stretch against Baylor, Oklahoma State and Kansas State, Withey looked like the best player on the floor for Kansas. First he dropped 25 points on the long, athletic front line of Baylor. He followed that performance with 18 points, 20 rebounds and seven blocks against Oklahoma State, then had a near triple-double against Kansas State.

Size rises as we get closer to the draft and more and more scouts seem to be convinced that given Withey's huge learning curve this season, he's destined to be a first-round pick, if not this year, then next. He's moved way up our Big Board the past few weeks and, with a strong run in March, could go even higher.

Nov 25 Update: Withey wasn't on very many draft boards coming into the tournament. But he's a mobile 7-footer who showed signs that he could be ready for a breakout season. He was a major factor for the Jayhawks against Duke on Wednesday. If he keeps up that learning curve, he's a possible second-round pick in the 2013 draft.
Withey is one of the best shot blockers in the draft. He doesn't really do much else, but he's a guy who should get 15 minutes a night as a solid backup.

No. 31: Cleveland Cavaliers

June 24 Update: Muscala might be the most underrated player in the draft. While his upside isn't huge -- the highest rating he received for our Secret NBA Draft Big Board was a 7 -- many teams believe he has the potential to be a solid stretch 4 in the NBA. His draft night range is 20 to 35.

May 27 Update: The big surprise of the workout was Muscala. While McCollum and Carter-Williams are both projected as top-10 picks, Muscala is on the first-round bubble.

His workout on Friday was extraordinary. It's no exaggeration to say that he missed two shots the entire workout. His skill set both around the basket (with an impressive jump hook) and facing the basket (especially from midrange out to the college 3-point line) was terrific. He has perfect form on his jump shot and a nice touch.

He showed the same shooting ability at the NBA draft combine last week, when he led all players with a 76 percent shooting percentage. Clearly he and Gonzaga's Kelly Olynyk are the most skilled big men in the draft and their college PERs back it up. Olynyk was ranked first and Muscala second in the nation in PER.

What concerns teams -- a little -- is Muscala's lack of strength in the post. He has a thin frame, isn't an elite athlete and isn't particularly long. However, he's so skilled, both around the basket and on the perimeter, that teams may try to make him a face-the-basket 4 at the next level.

I expect him to go somewhere between 15 and 35 on draft night. That's a pretty wide range, but it seems that teams are just now warming up to him. If he shoots it like that in workouts, he's going to rocket up draft boards.

Mar 20 Update: Muscala is one of the most polished big men in the game. He can score and rebound against anyone and sports one of the best Offensive Ratings in the country. What he needs is more quality games against athletic big men. I'm not sure the opening round against Butler, nor a potential Round of 32 matchup with Marquette really helps with that, however.

Jan 7 Update: When Jay and I put together our top 10 players in the country a few weeks ago, I debated back and forth between Virginia Tech's Erick Green and Muscala for that 10th spot. In retrospect, I wish I would've put Muscala there. You can make a strong argument that he is the best big man in the country. He's also not a bad NBA draft prospect, as he has good size (6-11, 234), can score inside and outside, is an excellent rebounder and a solid shot-blocker. He currently ranks second in the NCAA in PER. He could stand to add some strength and his lack of elite athleticism hurts him defensively, but if you watched what he did to Missouri on Saturday, you know that he can dominate the paint against anyone. Big men who can score, rebound and shoot free throws don't really come along that often in the NBA Draft. I could see Muscala ending up as a first-round pick in June.
Muscala is one of the more skilled players in the draft. I'm surprised he slid this far. Again, the Hawks grabbed a player who should have gone earlier considering the skill set.

No. 33: Cleveland Cavaliers

Jackson was the only player on the Big Board Top 30 to show up and play 5-on-5 at the Brooklyn workout. The move paid off. He stood out as the best player on the floor, and his confidence impressed the teams I spoke with there. His range right now is 21-35.

May 23 Update: Jackson was the only guy at the NBA draft workout in East Rutherford ranked in the top 30 -- and it showed. Virtually every GM I spoke with thought he was the best player in attendance. Not only did he show off his elite quickness and athletic ability, but he also showed off his floor general skills.

I was impressed with his ability to run the pick-and-roll. His speed allowed him to fly by defenders (Kentucky's Julius Mays was on him for most of the game), and he hit several big jumpers.

While his lack of size is an issue (he measured 5-foot-10½ in Chicago with just a 5-10 wingspan), he's an elite athlete (measured with a 42-inch vertical leap in New Jersey), a good scorer and a willing passer. We've had him ranked as a first-round pick for the past two months or so, and he vindicated that to a large degree. If a team is willing to look past the size issue, he has a great shot of going in the first round.

May 15 Update: Jackson is one guy who should do really well at the combine. He's an explosive athlete, shoots fairly well and has terrific speed. He's going to take a hit in the measurements department (there's almost no chance he's the 5-foot-10 at which he's listed), but everyone is expecting that. Interviews will be a big factor for him. Some teams appear to be a bit wary about his background, but from what I can gather, he's a good guy.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 25 pick, Los Angeles Clippers): The Clippers can't afford to keep Eric Bledsoe, so most likely he'll be traded this summer. The Clippers will need a cheap replacement, and Jackson could fill that need. Clippers fans will love Jackson, an elite athlete who plays with reckless abandon. He's got the potential to be another Nate Robinson.

May 2 Update: Jackson might be tiny (he's closer to 5-foot-8 than his listed 5-10) but he's one of the most explosive, well-rounded players in the draft. With Nate Robinson dressing down the Nets in the playoffs, I think it's going to be easier to make an argument for Jackson -- especially when you factor in that he's actually played like a point guard for much of the past season.

Apr 16 Update: Jackson might be small, but he's a ridiculous athlete who can score from anywhere on the floor. And man, did he finish the season strong, averaging 19.6 PPG and 11 APG in leading Baylor to the NIT championship. Other small point guards like Myck Kabongo and Phil Pressey also are in the mix here with Jackson, but a number of scouts have mentioned Jackson as a potential first-round pick.

Feb 12 Update: Jackson is creating some buzz for himself with his performance this season. Yes, he's undersized. But his elite athletic ability, his ability to score the ball from everywhere and his emerging point guard skills all have teams interested as a potential late first round pick.
I'm a big Jackson fan. He's an elite athlete, can score from anywhere and actually showed that he's a real point guard this season. At No. 42, it's another very good pick for the Sixers.

No. 46: Utah Jazz

Mar 20 Update: Wolters is one of the most electric guards in the country. If he were playing at a bigger school, he'd be invoking the Jimmer Fredette comparisons right and left. What he needs to secure a solid place in the draft is a big game against top competition, and he got it with the Jackrabbits' opening game. A head-to-head with Michigan's Trey Burke is exactly what every scout in America wants to see. If Wolters and South Dakota State can pull off the upset? Wolters might just sneak his way up to first-round territory.

Dec 10 Update: Wolters doesn't play in a big conference (Summit League), but his huge numbers for the second straight season can't be overlooked. He also has been pegged primarily as a scoring guard, but his 6.1 assists per game and nearly 3-1 assist-to-turnover ratio prove that he's more than just a scorer. While he has the most questionable NBA future of any player on this list, there are few players in the country more valuable to their teams than Wolters.

Dec 20, 2011 Update: We've been inundated with small-school point guards like Iona's Scott Machado (Top 100 Rank: 34), Weber State's Damian Lillard (Top 100 Rank: 46) and Long Beach State's Casper Ware (Top 100 Rank: 100) this season. It looks like we need to add a fourth one, South Dakota State's Nate Wolters (Top 100 Rank: 89) to the mix. Wolters just got done lighting up Washington for 34 points, seven assists and zero turnovers in an upset win. He's been doing stuff like that all season. While Wolters lacks the requisite hyper-athleticism of other elite point guards, he's got toughness, craftiness and fearlessness going for him. And at his size, he's able to score over smaller point guards. No one is talking about Wolters as a sure-fire first-rounder, but a number of scouts I've spoken with think he's got a real shot at the NBA.

The Wizards have traded this pick to the Bucks. I love Wolters; he was the Jimmer Fredette of college basketball this year, but because he was at South Dakota State, few got to see him play. He's a true point guard who also can really score the basketball. If he can defend anyone, he'll be another second-round steal.

No. 32: Oklahoma City Thunder

June 18 Update: Again, the Thunder have a ton of flexibility right now, and with two first-round picks they don't need a player to come over immediately. Abrines is an interesting player. He's playing limited minutes for one of the top teams in Europe and has significant upside. The team can afford to be patient and stash him in Europe for a year or two until he's ready to come in and contribute.

May 15 Update: Abrines won't be in Chicago, partly because his team just finished playing in the Euroleague Final Four. Abrines played just four minutes in the first game, but in Sunday's consolation game he played 19 minutes and scored 10 points. There was a significant collection of NBA scouts and GMs present, and they mostly walked away impressed. He could be a high riser on the board in the coming weeks.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 28 pick, San Antonio Spurs): Abrines actually is getting decent minutes for one of the best teams in Europe right now. He's a scorer who can get it going from wherever. Abrines is a major sleeper in my opinion, which is exactly the type of guy the Spurs always seem to find.

May 2 Update: Abrines could end up being the sleeper in this draft. The Spanish 2-guard has been playing -- and playing well -- on one of the best teams in Europe at the age of 20. A couple of international scouts I spoke with this week are convinced that he's the second-best European prospect behind Saric. There are questions about whether he's ready or willing to leave Barcelona, but if those are answered, he could be an excellent pick for a team in the second half of the first round.

Apr 29 Update: Abrines hasn't been able to do much this season. He's on an elite Barcelona team and hasn't seen much in the way of playing time. However, when he has played, he's been fantastic. He had 21 points in 21 minutes against Macabbi Tel Aviv in an April 4 Euroleague game. He followed that with 10 points in 14 minutes against Panathinaikos.

Abrines might be one of the best young scorers in Europe right now and has put up big numbers whenever he gets minutes. He's quick, is a good athlete and is gaining great experience in Euroleague play. He could be special.

Abrines was the best young talent left on the board. He reminds some of a young Rudy Fernandez. Abrines is a good scorer and shooter, and he's already is getting good minutes in the best league in Europe. In a year or two, this could turn out to be a very valuable pick. It's another steal for the Thunder.

No. 37: Detroit Pistons

May 15 Update: Everyone still wants to love Goodwin, but every time they go to the tape it's brutal. Goodwin is going to show well athletically, but what he really has to prove is that he's in the process of fixing a very broken jump shot.

May 8 Update (Projected No. 30 pick, Phoenix Suns via Miami Heat): This is a pure talent grab by the Suns. Goodwin has elite speed and quickness. But his wild shot selection and poor outside shooting contributed to Kentucky's woes this season. The Suns, however, can afford to be patient with him and wait to see if he develops.

May 2 Update: Goodwin remains an enigma to most scouts. They love his speed and athletic ability but are still trying to figure out how his game will translate to the NBA given his slight build, lack of height and poor shooting. But Goodwin has so much upside that it seems someone will take him in the first round.

Apr 1 Update: Goodwin announced on Monday that he will declare for the 2013 NBA Draft. Goodwin came into the season ranked as a potential lottery pick. He has great speed and is fearless taking it to the rack. Early in the season, Kentucky head coach John Calipari compared him a young Russell Westbrook. However, Goodwin's faults began to eclipse his strengths as the season wore on. His shot selection could be atrocious, his jump shot was flat and he struggled with toughness on both sides of the ball. He's now projected as a mid to late first-round pick. The upside is there, but teams will have to be patient with him.

Mar 26 Update: Goodwin actually stepped up (offensively at least) the last few games for Kentucky and put together some of his best performances of the season. Unfortunately, he still couldn't get his jump shot to fall and didn't hit a 3-pointer in his last three games. He's still a bit wild and turnover-prone, but the athletic ability and scoring knack are there. While he too is indicating he'll return for his sophomore season, there is very little chance of him starting with the Harrison twins arriving. Of the three Kentucky freshmen trying to figure things out, he might be the one most likely to leave. He's not close to being ready for the NBA, but he wouldn't be the first young guard drafted purely on potential.

Mar 13 Update: Goodwin is one of the most difficult players in the draft to peg at the moment. The athletic ability, the speed and a penchant for finishing at the basket are all there. His shooting woes have abated a bit the past few weeks, as well. But the poor decision-making, slight frame and inconsistency all point to his needing at least another year under John Calipari at Kentucky. Barring a Cinderella run in the NCAA tournament, will he return to school for his sophomore year?

Feb 27 Update: Goodwin broke out of a horrific shooting slump last week against both Vanderbilt and Missouri on Saturday. In fact, he hit his first 3-pointer (two of them, actually) since a game against Texas A&M on Jan. 12. Given that Goodwin is a shooting guard, that's not a good thing. He clearly has the athletic ability to be a dominant pro, but he's still wild and plays out of control (see his seven turnovers against Missouri). Someone will take him based on his raw talent, but he really needs another season at Kentucky.

Jan 30 Update: Goodwin can be an amazing finisher at the basket, but when he gets to the line, he falls apart. Over the past six games, Goodwin is just 32-for-50, or 64 percent. Combine that with a horrific 1-for-17 from 3-point range in his past seven games, and he's not doing a very good job of persuading NBA scouts that he can shoot the ball.

Dec 17 Update: Goodwin is an electric scorer and acrobatic finisher at the basket. Like a lot of players on this list, his lack of a clearly defined position has created doubts about his NBA game. And so has his erratic shot selection. But if he settles down and plays to his strengths, there is some Russell Westbrook in him.

Nov 15 Update: Calipari has been comparing Goodwin to a young Russell Westbrook. He has a ton of athletic ability, and no one in college basketball can stay in front of him. But he also seems to have inherited Westbrook's penchant for making bad basketball decisions when he's pressured. Some of the shots Goodwin has taken have been inspired dropped jaws, head shaking or both. Still, Goodwin has elite NBA athlete written all over him. If Calipari can rein him in? Again, top-10 pick.

Oct 11 Update: Goodwin might be the best pure scorer on this new Kentucky team. He's a strong, athletic wing who thrives on slashing to the basket. He's a terrific finisher at the rim and is a beast in transition. It's not a stretch to think that Goodwin could end up leading the Wildcats in scoring this season.

Goodwin will be several spots higher on the board if he can show scouts that he's got a consistent shot from beyond the 3-point line. He also will have to show that he's willing to play on the defensive end as well. He's young and has plenty of room for growth, and if Calapari can get him locked in, Kentucky could actually have more lottery picks this season than they did last season.

June 27 Update: He is a combination guard with NBA size who should have the ball in his hands quite a bit at Kentucky. Goodwin is terrific in the transition game because he can rebound down, take a bust-out dribble and go all the way to score or deliver an assist. Plus, he is one of the better dribble-drive players in the 2012 class because he can make plays for himself or teammates. However, he needs to polish up his long-range jumper and show he can make open 3s and shoot behind a ball screen.

On the defensive side, he can be very good keeping his man out of the lane while closing out on shooters and contesting shots. - by Paul Biancardi

The Warriors and Suns swapped picks, and Phoenix got the youngest American player in the draft. John Calipari compared him to a young Russell Westbrook -- he's an elite athlete and a creative finisher. If he could hit a jump shot, he would've gone much higher. If the Suns are patient, this could really pay off.
If the Suns are patient, this could really pay off.

April 17 Update: Jerrett has declared for the 2013 NBA Draft. Jerrett was ranked as one of the top-10 high school players in the country last year by ESPN, but he struggled as a freshman playing a supporting role off the bench. With several high-profile recruits coming to Arizona next year, Jerrett decided to cut bait. He intrigues NBA guys because of his ability to stretch the floor as a big. A potential second-round pick.

Mar 19 Update: the real action is with the Wildcats' three freshmen -- Tarczewski, Ashley and Jerrett. All three could be first-round picks in 2014. Of the three, Ashley has had the best season. He's an elite athlete learning how to play small forward. Tarczewski has the most upside as a big, athletic center who can run the floor, rebound and block shots. Jerrett is a stretch 4 in the mold of Ryan Anderson.

Mar 28, 2012 Update: Jerrett has been a bit of a late bloomer and has been shooting up the rankings this year. Jerrett is a stretch 4 who can spread the floor and score in the paint. He may not burst onto the scene immediately, but some scouts say he'll be the Wildcats' best player.

Portland traded Jerrett to Oklahoma City. He is a stretch four who was one of the top high school players in the country, but as a freshman at Arizona he often came off the bench. So he has more talent than his stats suggest and gives the Thunder another shooting threat.

No. 41: Memphis Grizzlies

Apr 28 Update: Roberson is a rebounding machine and that alone may get him drafted in the first round. Unfortunately, his offense still hasn't caught up with his defense right now. A potential first round to early second round pick.

Mar 20 Update: Roberson has long been a poster child for the advanced stat guys, but his inability to generate any offense this season has hurt his case somewhat. He's a great rebounder, but is he anything more than that?

Nov 30 Update: Last season, Roberson was a favorite of stat-heads everywhere. He was a beast on the boards and all he needed was some semblance of an offensive game. While he's proven he can still rebound the basketball, his offensive game has actually regressed a bit this season. Can a team justify taking him in the first round based on rebounding alone?

Oct 22 Update: Roberson, at 6-foot-7, is one of the best rebounders in college basketball. His elite athletic abilities, combined with a terrific motor and wiry strength, allow him to outquick opponents on the boards.

The big question for Roberson is position. NBA scouts want to see him make the transition to the 3 given his lack of ideal size, length or girth for an NBA power forward. While he showed some promise as a perimeter scorer last season, he still has a long ways to go before he can convince NBA teams that he's a legit 3 man. If he does show more offensive game this year, he'll move up 10 to 15 spots on our board.

But then again, maybe he won't have to. Kawhi Leonard had similar numbers and concerns coming out of college and was drafted just outside the lottery.

Apr 8 Update: Roberson is one of the best rebounders and defenders in college basketball. He reminds some scouts of Kawhi Leonard. If he can go back to school and continue to improve his offensive game, he's got a shot at being a mid to late first round pick in 2013.

Mar 6 Update: Roberson is one of the most underrated prospects in draft talks because no one is running to scout Colorado games (or Pac-12 games for that matter). But Roberson has quietly averaged a double-double for the season. He's an explosive leaper, a tough versatile defender and has a motor that doesn't stop.

His offensive game is still a work in progress, but he reminds many scouts of a poor man's Kawhi Leonard. Roberson, according to sources, would like to make the leap to the NBA next year if he can. He's going to need a strong tournament to get there. But given the bizarre state of the Pac-12, anything is possible.

April 15 Update: Roberson was one of the best rebounders per minute in college basketball as a freshman. Now that Alec Burks is gone, much of the scoring load will also fall on his shoulders. If he can pick up the slack there as well, he's a very intriguing prospect.

This pick went from the Wolves to the Warriors to the Thunder. Roberson was a stats-geek star. Our own Kevin Pelton ranked him as the third-best prospect in the draft based on his WARP model. Roberson is a bit of a tweener, but he's one of the best rebounders in the draft. Once again the Thunder try to prove they're smarter than the rest of us.
Bit of a tweener but a stats-geek star.

Apr 12 Update: Covington has been on the NBA radar for a while but struggled this season due in part to a knee injury. May 20 Update: Leslie's terrific athletic numbers reminded scouts he might be one of the three or four best athletes in the draft and alleviated fears that he wouldn't have the lateral quickness to guard shooting guards in the NBA. His combine-best 10.19-second score on the lane agility drill, combined with a huge vertical leap and a big wingspan, have teams curious. If he can go into workouts and shut down the other small forwards in the workouts, he's going to be a lock for the first round.

Apr 1 Update: Leslie declared for the 2013 NBA Draft on Monday. Leslie is an enigma to NBA scouts. Blessed with great length and athleticism, he's never quite been able to get over the hump with scouts despite putting up the solid numbers as both a sophomore and junior. He's been plagued with the idea of his upside and now that he's 21 and hasn't lived up to it, the bottom has started to fall out of his stock. After being ranked in our Top 30 for much of his freshman, sophomore and junior years, the last few months he's slipped into the second round on our Big Board. While it's possible he could sneak into the first, it's more likely he's a second-rounder at this point.

Jan 30 Update: Leslie remains a player plagued by the dreaded "upside" tag. As a freshman and sophomore, it usually helps more than it hurts. As a junior, the questions start pouring in. His 17-point, 10-rebound performance against North Carolina on Saturday and 20-point, 14-rebound game against Virginia showed us, once again, what he's capable of. But he needs to do it every night.

Oct 11 Update: Leslie has been an enigma since high school. Blessed with elite athletic abilities and size, the 6-foot-9 forward has the speed and quickness of a guard. He's a monster in transition and uses his quickness to beat bigger opponents of the dribble. He's coming off a pretty impressive sophomore campaign and scouts have high hopes. But he still has some convincing to do.

Leslie still can be frustratingly inconsistent. He doesn't always play hard, especially on defense. He also lacks a great perimeter game, which limits his offensive potential.

If his production can start to match his potential, he has the ability to be a lottery pick. But until he shows that drive and toughness every night, he's more likely to find himself somewhere between the mid- to late first round.

Apr 18 Update: Leslie announced that he was returning to school for his junior year. Leslie has always been a highly touted prospect among NBA scouts thanks to his excellent length and athleticism. As a sophomore, he began to show he's more than just an athlete and would've likely been a first-round pick had he declared for the draft. Next year, he should be the leader of a very stacked NC State team. If he continues to improve, he could go in the late lottery or mid-first round.

Mar 19 Update: Leslie came out of high school with a checkered rep. He was regarded as one of the most athletic prospects in his class. But his attitude and indifference on the court raised eyebrows. As a freshman he showed both his potential and his potholes. As a sophomore, Leslie has made major strides in his game and in his consistency.

For two straight games in the tournament, against San Diego State and Georgetown (and along with some stellar play in the ACC tournament against North Carolina and Virginia), Leslie carried the Wolfpack and now has them in the Sweet 16. Scouts love Leslie's length and athletic ability. But it's his newfound toughness and aggressiveness on the court that's led to them warming up quickly to him. Leslie still is a work in progress, but virtually every general manager I spoke with this weekend had him ranked somewhere in the late-teens to the 20s on their boards. His matchup against Thomas Robinson and Kansas on Friday should be one of the two best scouting scenes this weekend.

Mar 6 Update: After two seasons in college basketball, Leslie is still more prospect than player. He improved as a sophomore in virtually every area, but the improvement was incremental, not seismic the way some scouts expected.

Leslie has the length and athleticism to be a big-time pro. He's worked on his post game this season, but he still remains more comfortable on the perimeter. He'd need a big run in the NCAA tournament to move himself firmly into the first round.

Apr 15 Update: Internet reports have been suggesting for weeks that Leslie was returning to NC State for his sophomore season. He probably needs to. But in the past two weeks he's begun talking to agents. Leslie, like Kansas guard Josh Selby, may be seeing an opportunity here in a weak draft to sneak into the first round based soley on upside.

Mar 8 Update:Leslie is a super athletic, versatile phenom who many scouts privately said could be the best NBA prospect in his class last spring. Things haven't panned out the way Leslie had hoped this season. He and Tracy Smith were supposed to push the Wolfpack into contention in the ACC. Instead the team fell apart, and Leslie hasn't been great.

Scouts still love the length, athleticism and versatility in Leslie's game. But he lacks strength and a defined position, has given an inconsistent effort all season and never seemed like he could really help his team win.

I continue to hear that Leslie is leaning heavily toward declaring for the draft and, given his raw talent, someone is likely to take him in the first round. But a breakout game or two in the ACC tournament could do wonders for his draft stock. Scouts want to like him -- he just needs to give them a little more ammunition to work with.

Feb 8 Update: Leslie started the season strong but struggled to live up to much of the hype for the Wolfpack and eventually was demoted from the starting five, and then was suspended for the game against the Duke Blue Devils on Saturday for violating team rules.

Leslie has all the talent of a lottery pick but has been unable to put it all together on a consistent basis. His lack of a defined position along with his lack of strength has hurt both his college game and his draft stock. The word among NBA agents is that he's likely to declare as long as he's a first-round pick. He'll likely get a nod in the top-30 just on sheer upside, but it's looking like his days as a lottery pick are behind him.

Nov 24 Update, By David Thorpe: Coming into the season, Leslie looked to be a phenomenal athlete who would overwhelm opponents with sheer physical talent. That alone excites scouts and executives in the NBA, as that kind of advantage can pay dividends immediately while allowing for the growth of a player. It can unnerve decision-makers, though, especially if those gifts come in a package that is prone to inconsistent effort.

So Leslie, who is seen as a player who relaxes too often, has much to gain by competing as hard as he can on every play. Without doubt, a young player can learn to do that. I've liked what I've seen from him so far, especially his "silkiness" as a cutter (which reminds me of Chris Bosh). He's better at getting open than finishing, and if that part of his game improves scouts will more easily forgive his penchant for not hustling to the extreme. Of course, helping N.C. State win a lot and perhaps make a March run would help a raw player like him more than anything (think Tyrus Thomas). Athletic freaks are easier to fall in love with in that kind of setting.

Nov 16 Update: Leslie is one of the biggest "upside" freshmen in the country. He can jump out of the gym, flies up and down the floor and has an element of "spectacular" to his game. He's also a guy that scouts feel may need a little more time to develop a consistent offensive game.

Leslie came out of the gates humming. He scored 21 points, grabbed 6 boards and blocked 6 shots in his debut for the Wolfpack.

Said one scout, "He's got so many tools to be an awesome NBA player. If he figures it all out this year, he's a top-five pick."

Oct 21 Update Leslie is another athletic freak whose physical abilities immediately translate at the NBA level. Leslie runs the floor like a guard, can jump out of the gym and can defend multiple positions on the floor. Unfortunately, like most super athletes, Leslie lacks any refinement in his game at the moment. He doesn't have a defined position, lacks reliable post moves and is an inconsistent perimeter player.

Leslie is one of those players who could, with a breakout year, be a top-three pick based on potential. He could also struggle and slip entirely out of the first round. It's really anyone's guess at this point. We've split the difference and have him in the late lottery, but we should know pretty soon which direction he's going to lean this season.

Jun 25 Update: In 2011, we have a whopping nine freshmen projected as one-and-done lottery picks, including UNC's Harrison Barnes, Baylor's Perry Jones, North Carolina State's C.J. Leslie, Kansas' Josh Selby, Duke's Kyrie Irving, Ohio State's Jared Sullinger and Kentucky's Brandon Knight, Terrence Jones and Enes Kanter.

June 20 Update: Leslie is a bit of an enigma. He's more athlete than basketball player at the moment, but the physical gifts he has are undeniable. Teams already love him for his defensive presence. If he adds some muscle to that frame and shows some improvement on the offensive end, he could go very, very high.

May 7 Update: If Brown were a more consistent jump shooter, he would be a lottery pick.

As it is, the 6-5 junior has enough of the other attributes needed to be a solid NBA rotation player that he should be able to stick in the league no matter where he gets selected. In the last two seasons, Brown has been one of the most effective playmakers in the country with excellent size, passing skills and deceptive athleticism, especially in the open court. This season he had nine games of 10 assists or more for the Wolfpack.

What I love about Brown is that he can play point guard at various speeds. In NC State's UCLA half-court offense, he was charged with making sure that he distributed the ball equally among four double-figure scorers in addition to looking for his own shot (averaging 12.4 PPG himself). And Brown was comfortable playing in an up-tempo game.

There are two major question marks about Brown's game, and they are interrelated -- his outside shooting and his ability to play in screen-and-roll action.

After shooting 35 percent behind the arc as a sophomore, it dropped to 26 percent this season. In fact, after spraining an ankle at Virginia in late January, Brown made just seven of his last 38 3-point shots. On the bright side, he did shoot 77 percent from the free throw line this season, so there is a chance he will be able to acquire a solid shooting stroke with hard work.

Because just 11 percent of the Wolfpack's half-court offense involved screen-and-roll plays, Brown did not have many opportunities to hone his skills in ball-screen offense -- something he will need to do at the NBA level. He has the aptitude, and with repetitions, he could be very good in that area, where an improved shooting stroke is a must. His ability to be a scoring threat will be critical to opening up screen-and-roll opportunities for his teammates.

NC State struggled to meet the high expectations set for it this season in the preseason polls, and there's likely plenty of blame to go around. But if that's what causes Brown's draft stock to drop after a junior season averaging 12 points and 7 assists per game, well & one team is getting a steal on draft night, especially if he polishes up a couple of key areas.

Mar 28 Update: Brown inspires a bit of a love/hate relationship among NBA scouts. He has great size for his position, is a good athlete and averaged over seven assists per game this year. At times he can play like an obvious first-round pick. But his lack of consistency on the floor, his poor shooting percentages, combined with several back-to-back disappointing seasons for his team give scouts pause. NBA teams want their point guards to be able to lead and for whatever reason, the Wolfpack haven't been able to string together a dominant season despite having plenty of NBA talent on the floor.

Jan 30 Update: Brown has been just as up-and-down as Leslie this season. When he's good, such as his 20-point, 11-assist performance against North Carolina, he can be really good. But when he's struggling (see the Clemson game), he still looks like he has a ways to go.

Nov 30 Update: Billed by many scouts as the best point guard in the draft before the season began, Brown has been anything but in the early going. He's shooting 34 percent from the field, 10 percent from 3-point range and averaging a career high 3.8 turnovers per game. Brown got completely abused by both Oklahoma State freshman Marcus Smart and Michigan sophomore Trey Burke the past few games. The scouts on his bandwagon are fighting each other for the remaining life rafts.

Oct 9 Update: NBA scouts are scouring college practices for standout point guards and over the past few weeks, I'm hearing a general buzz toward Brown. He still has flaws, lots of them, but he's got great size for his position and dramatically improved his sophomore season. If he can make the same improvements over the course of his junior year, he has the potential to be a late lottery to mid-first round pick.
I'm a little surprised Brown slid this far. He has great size for his position and showed this season he was a true point guard. He just can't shoot, sort of like Ricky Rubio.

Mar 15 Update: It was a tough final game for McCallum. He had just five points on 1-for-7 shooting in a bad loss to Wright State. Scouts have really warmed to McCallum this season, but he might need to consider returning to school for his senior year. He still is firmly on the first-round bubble.

Feb 11 Update: One thing that virtually all of these mid-major players have in common is high basketball IQ. McCallum is another player who thrives, in part, because he has such a superior feel for the game. He's very quick, can be a defensive hawk and thinks pass first. He needs to improve as a shooter, but given the way he has matured this season, his game has very few holes. I think he's the sleeper point guard of the draft, and I wouldn't be shocked at all to see his name called in the first round.

Nov 17 Update: McCallum didn't really wow anyone as a freshman, but NBA scouts are expecting a lot more from him this season now that he's settled in at Detroit.

McCallum is one of the few pure point guards in the country. He's a quick, pass-first sort of guard who is constantly managing the team on the court. McCallum needs to improve his jump shot and slow down on occasion, but he has the talent to have a breakout season.

Nov 2, 2010 Update: There are a number of players we could've put here. BYU's Jimmer Fredette has the best national reputation. Butler's Shelvin Mack has drawn a lot of praise from scouts. And Memphis has several players, including Wesley Witherspoon and freshman Will Barton, who should get attention from NBA scouts. But the scouts I spoke with are all the most intrigued by McCallum.

McCallum is a pure point guard who plays the game with his head and his heart. He surprised a lot of recruiters by turning down offers from UCLA and Florida to play for his father at Detroit Mercy.

McCallum's basketball IQ and floor leadership are off the charts. He's got sneaky speed and explosiveness and he's going to come in and dominate from day one. He may not be the type to be a one-and-done guard, but several NBA scouts say he could be a lottery pick down the road.

June 27 Update: McCallum decided to forgo playing for teams like UCLA and Florida to go play with his dad at Detroit. It was a controversial decision, but one that could ultimately pay off if he has a great freshman year at Detroit.

The Kings wanted a point guard, and McCallum is one of the purest point guards in the draft. He's not the sexist pick, but he's a steady floor leader who is very unselfish. If the Kings clean house, McCallum could end up playing a lot of minutes.

Mar 28 Update: Young has declared for the 2013 NBA Draft. Young was poised to be a possible lottery pick at the start of the season. Teams loved his size, athleticism and his scoring ability as a combo guard. However, Young struggled to live up to the promise of his freshman year. While his numbers are virtually identical across the board, his shooting percentages plummeted as a sophomore and by the end of the season he was no longer in the starting lineup for Arkansas. Young is now considered a bubble first rounder by scouts.

Mar 15 Update: Young was projected as a potential lottery pick at the start of the season, but his uneven play, an eventual benching and his lack of progress at the point guard position have hurt his stock tremendously. He still has his moments, like a big 27-point performance against Missouri last week. But the truth was that Young actually regressed a bit this season and has created huge question marks about his NBA potential. He's no longer a lock for the first round and has to consider returing to Arkansas for his junior year.

Jan 30 Update: There was a time when Young looked like the favorite to be the first point guard taken. He's been solid as a sophomore, but his shooting woes (0-for-9 from 3 and 13-for-39 from the field) in his past three games, combined with low assist totals, have NBA scouts wary that he's a high-volume, low-efficiency scorer -- and not a point guard.

Dec 14 Update: Scouts were all over the place on Young last year, and it doesn't appear much has changed. Some love his scoring acumen and peg him as a young Jamal Crawford. Others think he's a tweener with a selfish attitude and have him out of the first round. Young's performance this season has been a mild disappointment. His numbers are up across the board as expected, but his shooting stroke has left him. At the end of the day, Young was a bubble first rounder last year and a potential lottery pick this year. Unless he's awful in SEC play, it still looks like he made the right call to stay in school.

Oct 11 Update: Young is coming off a strong freshman season. But no one on this list inspires more debate among NBA scouts. Some scouts love him. They see him as a combo guard who can score the ball effectively and play both backcourt positions. Others see him as an undersized 2 who lacks the instincts to play the point.

Young was an efficient scorer as a freshman. He shot over 50 percent from the field and 41 percent from 3-point range. He also was effective at getting to the line. However, he played primarily off the ball and his assist-to-turnover ratio wasn't very impressive when he tried to run the team.

With a full season under his belt, many scouts feel he has the potential to be the best point guard in the draft if he can cut down on turnovers and get his teammates more involved. If he does prove to be a point, he's going to move up another notch or two on the board. This draft is devoid of great point-guard prospects and if Young can prove he's a playmaker, he'll be in high demand next June.

April 10 Update: Young is an explosive combo guard who is coming off a very impressive freshman season at Arkansas. Young was Arkansas' leading scorer for the season, shot 41 percent from three and showed he had the quickness and athleticism to get to the basket at will. He can be turnover prone and some scouts will question whether he can run the point full time in the pros, but had Young played for an elite school, he'd be ranked 10 to 15 points higher on our board. If he had stayed in the draft, we had him projected as a late first-round pick. In 2013 he could be a late lottery pick, especially if he starts running the point full time.

Mar 9 Update: Young is a talented scorer who can play both positions in the backcourt. Normally he's the type of player who stays another year in school, but with a very weak point guard crop this year, he might decide to come out. He's not ready, but that won't stop someone from taking him in the first round.

Mar 6 Update: In an otherwise depressing season for Arkansas fans, Young has been a standout. The 6-foot-3 combo guard from St. Louis has put together a fantastic freshman season. He shot 50 percent from the field, 42 percent from 3-point range and showed he could get to the basket at will. If he played for Kentucky or North Carolina, scouts would have him ranked as a lottery pick.

As it is, Young and the Razorbacks are in danger of getting knocked out in the first round of the SEC tournament against LSU. If they can get by LSU, however, they would face Kentucky in the next round and give Young the stage he needs to impress scouts. It's hard to believe the Razorbacks would get past the Wildcats -- so this is the equivalent of a Final Four game for Young. Arkansas played Kentucky only once all season and Young wasn't great. A big couple of games for Young in front of key decision-makers could move him firmly into the first round.

Dec 13 Update: Keep an eye on Young (Rank: 49). Young didn't get the hype of some of the other elite freshmen in the country, but he's quietly putting together a huge season for the Razorbacks. This super-quick combo guard can get to the basket at will, but it's been his stellar shooting that is turning teams' heads.

Mar 31 Update: Young is a quick, athletic guard that flies in the open court and can get to the rim at will. He should inject a lot of life into Arkansas's offense next year. A potential first round pick.

Apr 12 Update: Kabongo announced that he's declaring for the 2013 NBA Draft. Kabongo had to sit out the first 23 games of the season due to an NCAA infraction, so his stock has taken a pretty devastating blow going from a potential lottery pick to the first-round bubble. In the 11 games he did play, Kabongo dramatically upped his scoring average, but his turnovers were up, too. Plus his jump shot, which he was supposedly working on all year, just wasn't falling. Scouts are torn on Kabongo. Some still see the guy who was ranked as a potential Top 10 pick out of high school. They believe the situation at Texas was toxic and that he'd still be a lottery pick had he played elsewhere. Others think he is too small and was just exposed in college. He could go anywhere from the mid-first round to the early-second round.

Apr 2 Update: Kabongo's stock took a huge hit when he was forced to miss most of the season because of NCAA sanctions. He played well, for the most part, averaging 14.6 PPG and 5.3 APG. However, his turnovers were up and his shooting percentages were way down. He clearly was still getting his legs underneath him. Nevertheless, scouts continue to see promise in him, and if he declares for the draft, could be snatched up in the second half of the first round by a team in need of a point guard.

Mar 8 Update: Kabongo is the most intriguing player on this list for me. After sitting out the first 23 games thanks to an NCAA suspension, he's come back for the final few weeks of Texas' season and has been, for the most part, great. With the exception of a rough game against Oklahoma State last weekend, Kabongo has proved to be an efficient scorer and passer and has looked like a first-round pick. If he could get Texas past the first few rounds of the Big 12 tournament, he still has a chance to move way up our Big Board. Scouts really love the talent. They just need to see a little more.

Dec 21 Update: Poor Kabongo. He seriously flirted with bolting for the NBA last year and ultimately decided to come back to school. Then the NCAA stepped in, declared him guilty until proven innocent and tabled his trial for the first half of the season. No one seems to know what's going on or why it's taking the NCAA so long to figure out who paid for him to fly to Cleveland last summer to work out with a basketball trainer (the horror!). Kabongo is a bit of a cautionary tale for young prospects. The messages the NCAA and teams send are so muddled. He was trying to get the best info he could about whether to stay in school, ultimately decides to return and is punished for allegedly taking money from an agent to do a workout. Whether he did or didn't get the money from an agent, the punishment itself has already gone overboard. Meanwhile, with every game he sits, he loses money. This week the NCAA ruled that he would be ineligible the entire year, then, on appeal, changed the suspension to 23 games -- meaning he'll return in mid February. He wasn't great as a freshman, and without him on the court, other players are passing him on the Big Board.

Oct 18 Update: Kabongo entered Texas with the reputation as the best point guard in his recruiting class. As a freshman he struggled mightily playing alongside resident ball hog J'Covan Brown.

Kabongo seriously considered declaring for the NBA draft last year, but eventually was persuaded that another year in Austin would improve his draft status.

Scouts are cautiously optimistic. Kabongo is long and quick, and he can really see the floor. He may be the best pure point guard in the draft. He has some young talent around him this season. If he can take the reins of the team, hit his jumpers and turn Texas back into a winner, his stock will skyrocket. (Of course, there is the possibility that the NCAA investigation into his relationship with LeBron James' agent will complicate things.)

There's been a major drought of point guards the past few years. Kabongo is one of the few in the 2013 draft who has the talent to be an NBA starter someday.

Mar 26 Update: Kabongo flirted with declaring for the draft, but made the right decision to return to school. He has the potential to be a late lottery pick next year if he shows improvement at Texas. Had he declared for the draft this year, he would have been stuck on the first-round bubble.

Mar 13 Update: The Good: Kabongo is a pure playmaker who can make everyone around him better. He's quick and he has a pretty nice jump shot.

The Bad: Pure point guards need talent around them. Kabongo had a black hole -- J'Covan Brown and little else. He struggled in virtually every area as a freshman.

The Upside: Kabongo is a much better prospect than he showed as a freshman at Texas. It just wasn't a great fit for him this year after most of Texas' talent left for the NBA. His stock has slid considerably because of it, but it wouldn't take him long to rebuild faith in his skills. This is a very weak point guard draft, and Kabongo is one of the few point guards in the NCAA with the ability to make an impact at the next level.

Mar 9 Update: Kabongo came into the season hyped as, potentially, the best point guard in his freshman class. For the most part he struggled, particularly with his shot and with making a difference on the floor. Texas probably needs a win against Missouri on Friday to eke its way into the tournament. Kabongo is a talent ... but he's a talent that really needs to stay in school one more year.

Oct. 20 Update: This year's draft might be the weakest we've seen in years at the point guard position. Only two point guards are in serious contention for a lottery pick -- Kabongo and Kentucky freshman Marquis Teague. Teague is a super-athletic slasher. Kabongo is a pure, unselfish point guard who makes everyone around him better.

Kabongo's lack of size and lack of a great surrounding class in Texas this year are knocks against him. But NBA teams need point guards every year and pure point guards with very few weaknesses are very hard to come by.

Mar 31 Update: Kabongo is the closest thing this freshman class has to a pure point guard. He sees the floor well and is an excellent leader on the court. He's a bit undersized, but has terrific potential. The biggest question is how he'll fit next to Cory Joseph.
