Apr 5 Update: Thomas has declared for the 2013 NBA Draft. Thomas is an elite scorer who can do damage near the basket or on the perimeter. But he make scouts a little wary because of his lack of elite athletic ability, he's a 'tweener stuck between the 3 and the 4 and his indifference on the defensive end. He can put the ball in the bucket, but they'll want to see more than that if he's going to be a first-round prospect. He's a bubble first-rounder right now, in the 25-40 range.

Apr 2 Update: Thomas might be the best pure scorer in the Big Ten, and he had a strong performance for the Buckeyes in virtually every game. He averaged 21.8 ppg, shot better than 50 percent from the field, and was 8-for-19 from beyond the arc. He clearly is a gifted scorer, has a NBA body and is a beast getting to the basket. So why isn't he slated to go in the first round?

A couple of issues hurt Thomas' NBA potential. One, he's not a great athlete. Second, he's a bit of a tweener at the next level. He's probably a small forward but would struggle to defend them due to a lack of foot speed and lack of overall intensity at the defensive end. Thomas, scouts believe, is a one-dimensional player who may struggle to put up the same results at the next level. While scouts clearly see him as a potential second-round pick, I couldn't find any scouts or GMs who had him in their top 30 at the moment.

He, too, struggled in Pelton's adjusted WARP model, with a score of 0.2, putting him at No. 57 among our Top 100.

Mar 19 Update: Thomas is one of the best scorers in college basketball, but his lack of elite athleticism and his porous defense have kept him mired in the second round.

Oct 25 Update: Thomas has a chance to be one of the top scoring forwards in college basketball this season. He can score from anywhere on the floor and has proved in two seasons at Ohio State that he isn't afraid to let the ball fly. Thomas can play multiple positions on offense and provides mismatch options at both the 2, 3 and 4. If he played any defense at all, or if he was a better athlete, Thomas would be much higher in our rankings. He showed up this summer in the best shape of his career. If he can lead Ohio State deep into the tournament, he could end up hearing his name called in the first round.

Apr 6 Update: Thomas announced that he's returning to Ohio State for his junior season. Thomas is one of the best scorers in college basketball and already has an NBA body. What he still needs is to show scouts he's willing to give the same effort on the defensive end as the offensive end. He would've been a bubble first-round pick had he declared this year. Look for him to project as a mid-to-late first-rounder in 2013.

Jan 3 Update: Thomas (Top 100 Rank: 61) might be one of the better volume scorers in college basketball, but his inability to guard anyone has created a quandary for coach Thad Matta and NBA scouts. Thomas' lack of lateral quickness is partly to blame. But watch him and the lack of effort is just as big of a problem. NBA teams always need scorers, but Thomas' poor defensive play is giving them pause.

Nov 3 Update: Thomas is an offensive powerhouse who spent most of his freshman year coming off the bench. This year, he should have a significantly expanded role on the Buckeyes and could be one of those players that immediately doubles his scoring average next season. As a freshman, Thomas wasn?t just a scorer, he also proved himself to be a terrific rebounder on both ends of the floor.

The question for Thomas is two fold. One, does he have the athletic ability necessary to defend his position at the NBA level? Just as important, does he have the willpower to get into great shape, play hard all the time and prove to scouts he wants to do this. If he has a big year, someone might be willing to take that gamble.

Nov 16 Update: Jared Sullinger got of the attention when he committed to the Buckeyes, but in his first game, Thomas showed he may be a force to be reckoned with as well. Thomas had 24 points, 8 boards and shot 67 percent from 3-point range in his college debut.

Thomas had a rep as one of the best pure scorers in high school basketball his senior year and he really lived up to it in his first game. His strength, athletic ability, versatility and excellent shooting stroke make him a very difficult guy to guard. We may have initially ranked him lower than he deserves.

June 25 Update: Thomas hasn't gotten the hype of soon-to-be teammate Jared Sulligner, but he's one of the best pure scorers in the country. Could be a big time impact freshman.
Thomas was one of the best scorers in college basketball -- he can get his shot from anywhere. If he played any defense at all, he would have gone much higher.

Mar 7 Update: Kelly is coming off the best week of his career. Hampered by a foot injury that cost him 13 games this season, Kelly returned in time to take on Miami and played one of the greatest games in Duke history. Kelly scored 36 points on 10-for-14 shooting, went 7-for-9 from 3 and helped Duke win a huge game at home.

Overall, Kelly is having a terrific season and has proved to be the most important player on this season's Duke squad. His 131.9 ORtg is the sixth highest in the nation.

Kelly has been an acquired taste for NBA scouts. Scouts have tended to focus on what he doesn't do well (rebound, defend, so-so athletic ability). But at 6-foot-11, Kelly has shown real promise as a shooter with deep range and accuracy (he's shooting 53 percent from 3-point range this season). He also shows off a high basketball IQ, good ballhandling abilities and a surprisingly effective game in the post.

NBA GMs love stretch 4s, and Kelly's size and shooting ability make him an intriguing prospect. Whether Kelly will be able to produce enough points to mask his defensive deficiencies is a legit question. But I've begun to hear NBA scouts talk about him as a late-first-round prospect for the first time since early last season.

Jan 7 Update:: How can a player from Duke -- who we see on television more often than Wolf Blitzer -- be underrated? Kelly's contributions to Duke's success and the way the team plays is not often discussed -- and is often misunderstood. Kelly is a true "stretch 4," which is a term that is often misused to describe a forward who can make a perimeter shot. A lot of teams have great spacing, but floor spacing is only worth something if the defense goes with each player. If you can stretch the defense, you've got something, and Kelly can stretch the defense. He is a terrific shooter, can drive and is a good ball handler and passer. Even though he is not a great run-and-jump athlete, he is a very good defender who can block a shot and defend a post or perimeter big.

Nov 25, 2011 Update: I kept joking all week, via Twitter, that Rockets GM Daryl Morey was in love with Kelly. Since Morey can't talk to me about potential draft prospects, I was obviously kidding. But Kelly is a Morey type of player. Kelly, who won MVP honors in Maui, can stretch the floor, drive to the basket, play a little defense and make a lot of smart plays. Kelly needs to get stronger, become a better rebounder and he's never going to be an elite athlete, but there are spots in the NBA for 6-foot-10 mobile forwards who can stretch the floor. Coach K said after Wednesday's game that Kelly will be a pro. I can't really disagree, though I don't really see him reaching that status until the 2013 draft.

Kelly fits the big man mold Lakers coach Mike D'Antoni loves. He can shoot, can handle the ball and plays with a great basketball IQ. D'Antoni will be able to maximize his talents. It's a great fit for him and the Lakers.

Dec 31 Update: Murphy is not a first-round pick. Rather, he is a Matt Bonner-type NBA prospect who will not light up draft boards, but will be a valuable member of a winning NBA team. He can stretch the floor and make simple, smart plays, and he can blend in with others. Murphy has NBA range on his shot and can play pick-and-pop, but he can also roll down into the post and make a quick, simple move when he has a size advantage. He is primarily a stand-still jump shooter, but at his size, he can get his shot off quickly and he has improving strength. Murphy is not an NBA athlete and may have question marks on the defensive end, but he is an NBA player. If the focus is on what he cannot do, you will raise questions. If it remains on what he can do, he will be a productive player on a good team that values his skills and ability to be a spoke in a winning wheel.

Murphy is another of the en vogue stretch 4s. He can really shoot the basketball, and the Bulls can ask him to just spot up in the corners. He doesn't do much else, but his shooting alone makes him a valuable pick.
